a: ab, ā (prep. + abl.) — from, away from; by (ā before consonants)
ab: ab, ā (prep. + abl.) — from, away from; by
ac: atque, ac — and, and also (ac before consonants)
ad: ad (prep. + acc.) — to, toward; at, near
aeneas: Aenēās, -ae (m.) — Aeneas, Trojan prince, son of Venus and Anchises (nom. sg.)
altum: altus, -a, -um — high; deep; altum (n.) as noun, the deep sea, the open sea (n./m. acc. sg.)
animos: animus, -ī (m.) — mind, spirit; temper, passion (acc. pl.)
ante: ante (prep. + acc., adv.) — before, in front of; previously
argis: Argī, -ōrum (m. pl.) — Argos, Greek city; the Greeks (abl./dat. pl.)
arma: arma, -ōrum (n. pl.) — arms, weapons; war (acc./nom. pl.)
casus: cāsus, -ūs (m.) — fall; chance, misfortune, disaster (acc./nom. pl.; nom. sg.)
compagibus: compāgēs, -is (f.) — joint, seam, framework (of a hull) (abl./dat. pl.)
constitit: cōnsistō, cōnsistere, cōnstitī — to halt, take one's stand (3rd sg. perf.)
cum: cum — (conj.) when, since, although; (prep. + abl.) with
cunctus: cūnctus, -a, -um — all, the whole (m. nom. sg.)
das: dō, dare, dedī, datum — to give, grant (2nd sg. pres.)
dedit: dō, dare, dedī, datum — to give; to grant (+ inf.) (3rd sg. perf.)
dehinc: dehinc (adv.) — from here; then, next (one syllable in verse)
dum: dum (conj.) — while; until (+ subj., of a goal looked forward to)
enim: enim (conj., postpositive) — for, indeed, in fact
erat: sum, esse, fuī — to be (3rd sg. impf.)
et: et — and; also, even; et… et: both… and
fas: fās (n., indecl.) — what is right by divine law; fās est, it is right, it is permitted
fata: fātum, -ī (n.) — fate, destiny; pl. the fates (nom./acc. pl.)
fatis: fātum, -ī (n.) — fate, destiny; pl. the fates (abl./dat. pl.)
fatur: for, fārī, fātus sum — to speak, say (3rd sg. pres., deponent)
furor: furor, furōris (m.) — rage, frenzy, madness (nom. sg.)
genitor: genitor, genitōris (m.) — father, begetter; here Neptune (nom. sg.)
gente: gēns, gentis (f.) — race, people, nation (abl. sg.)
gentem: gēns, gentis (f.) — race, people, nation (acc. sg.)
haec: hic, haec, hoc — this; haec (n. pl.), these things, these words (n. nom./acc. pl.; f. nom. sg.)
hic: hīc (adv.) — here; hic, haec, hoc (pron.), this (m. nom. sg.)
hinc: hinc (adv.) — from here, hence; from this
his: hic, haec, hoc — this; pl. these (dat./abl. pl.)
hoc: hic, haec, hoc — this (n. nom./acc. sg.; m./n. abl. sg.)
hominum: homō, hominis (m.) — human being, man (gen. pl.)
iam: iam (adv.) — now, already; iam… iam, now… now
ille: ille, illa, illud — that; he, that man (m. nom. sg.)
illi: ille, illa, illud — that; illī, they, those (m. nom. pl.); to him/her (dat. sg.)
illum: ille, illa, illud — that; him, that man (m. acc. sg.)
imperio: imperium, -ī (n.) — command, authority, rule, empire (abl./dat. sg.)
in: in (prep.) — + acc. into, onto, against; + abl. in, on
ingens: ingēns, ingentis — huge, enormous, mighty (nom. sg.)
insequitur: īnsequor, īnsequī, īnsecūtus sum — to follow, follow on, come next (3rd sg. pres.)
italiam: Ītalia, -ae (f.) — Italy (acc. sg.; first syllable long in verse)
iuno: Iūnō, Iūnōnis (f.) — Juno, queen of the gods (nom. sg.)
latio: Latium, -ī (n.) — Latium, the region of central Italy round Rome (dat./abl. sg.)
longe: longē (adv.) — far, far off; by far
longo: longus, -a, -um — long, deep, far-reaching (m./n. abl./dat. sg.)
magno: magnus, -a, -um — great, large, loud (m./n. abl./dat. sg.)
mediis: medius, -a, -um — middle, mid-, in the midst of (m./n. abl./dat. pl.)
moenia: moenia, -ium (n. pl.) — walls, city walls (nom./acc. pl.)
montis: mōns, montis (m.) — mountain (gen. sg.; also acc. pl., = montēs)
multa: multus, -a, -um — much, many; multa (n. pl.) as noun, many things (n. acc./nom. pl.; f. nom./abl. sg.)
murmure: murmur, murmuris (n.) — murmur, rumble, roar (abl. sg.)
nec: nec, neque — and not, nor; nec… nec, neither… nor
ob: ob (prep. + acc.) — because of, on account of
olim: ōlim (adv.) — once, formerly; one day, in time to come
omni: omnis, -e — all, every, whole (abl. sg.; dat. sg.)
ora: ōs, ōris (n.) — mouth, face; pl. faces, features (acc./nom. pl.)
pectore: pectus, pectoris (n.) — breast, chest; heart (abl. sg.)
per: per (prep. + acc.) — through, across, throughout; by
post: post (adv.; prep. + acc.) — afterwards, hereafter; after, behind
potuit: possum, posse, potuī — to be able, can (3rd sg. perf.)
premit: premō, premere, pressī, pressum — to press, press down, hold in check (3rd sg. pres.)
pulchra: pulcher, pulchra, pulchrum — beautiful, lovely (f. abl./nom. sg.)
quae: quī, quae, quod — who, which (rel., f. nom. sg.; f./n. nom./acc. pl.)
quem: quī, quae, quod — who, whom (rel. or interrog., m. acc. sg.) · quis, quid after sī, nē — any(one), some(one) (indef., m. acc. sg.: sī quem)
qui: quī, quae, quod — who, which (rel. pron., m. nom. sg./pl.)
quibus: quī, quae, quod — who, which (rel., abl./dat. pl.)
quid: quis, quid — who, what (interrog., n. nom./acc. sg.)
quo: quī, quae, quod — who, which, what (rel. or interrog., m./n. abl. sg.); quō (adv.), where to
quoque: quoque (adv.) — also, too (follows the word it stresses)
refert: referō, referre, rettulī, relātum — to bring back; to reply, utter (3rd sg. pres.)
rerum: rēs, reī (f.) — thing, matter; pl. circumstances, fortunes (gen. pl.)
sanguine: sanguis, sanguinis (m.) — blood; descent, lineage (abl. sg.)
sceptra: scēptrum, -ī (n.) — sceptre; royal power (acc./nom. pl., often for sg.)
se: suī (reflexive pron.) — himself, herself, itself, themselves (acc.; also abl. sē)
secum: sē + cum — with himself/herself/themselves; to oneself
sic: sīc (adv.) — so, thus, in this way
sidera: sīdus, sīderis (n.) — star, constellation; pl. the sky (acc./nom. pl.)
sinus: sinus, -ūs (m.) — curve, bay, hollow, fold (acc. pl.; nom./acc. sg.)
sub: sub (prep.) — + abl. under, beneath; + acc. up to, under
summo: summus, -a, -um — highest, topmost; surface of (m./n. abl./dat. sg.)
super: super (adv. and prep.) — above, over; besides, in addition
talia: tālis, -e — such, of such a kind; tālia, such things, such words (n. acc./nom. pl.)
tempestatesque: tempestās, tempestātis (f.) — storm, tempest; season, weather (acc./nom. pl.) + -que 'and'
teucrorum: Teucrī, -ōrum (m. pl.) — the Teucrians, Trojans (from Teucer, an early king of Troy) (gen. pl.)
tibi: tū, tuī — you (sg.); tibi, to/for you (dat.)
troes: Trōs, Trōis (m.) — a Trojan (nom. pl., Greek form Trōes)
troia: Trōius, -a, -um — Trojan, of Troy (f. nom. sg.; n. nom./acc. pl.)
tum: tum (adv.) — then, at that time; next
vasto: vastus, -a, -um — vast, huge, desolate (m./n. abl./dat. sg.)
vertice: vertex, verticis (m.) — peak, summit; whirl (abl. sg.)
vi: vīs (f.; acc. vim, abl. vī) — force, power, violence (abl. sg.)
vos: tū, vōs — you (2nd pers. pl. pron.) (nom./acc. pl.)
